title: Resource Entitlement Reconciliation and Burst Management
author: Aisha Kumar
body:
Overview
---
This document defines the processes, telemetry anchors, automated reconciliation jobs, and manual runbooks used to: (1) reconcile tenant resource entitlements against observed consumption, and (2) manage controlled short-term "burst" capacity for private deployments (VPC and on‑prem). It is intended for SREs, Field Engineers, Platform Eng, and Customer Success teams responsible for private deploy steady‑state operations.

Scope
---
- Applies to Redwood Private control plane and tenant-serving runtime for all private/VPC/on‑prem customers.
- Covers entitlement accounting, periodic reconciliation, overage detection, burst admission, and capacity reallocation.
- Excludes initial provisioning (handled by install/playbook) and long‑term capacity purchases (handled by sales/finance).

Definitions
---
- Entitlement: configured reservation in tenant metadata (GPUs, vCPU equivalents, max qps, concurrent sessions).
- Observed consumption: 1m/5m/1h aggregated telemetry from serving-runtime, tenant-controller and billing-collector.
- Burst window: short time interval where a tenant may exceed entitlement up to a limit (default 15 minutes).
- Burst credit: accumulated allowance based on historical underutilization and contractual terms.

Principles
---
- Reconciliation is authoritative: entitlement in control-plane metadata + signed contract overrides runtime heuristics.
- Telemetry anchors are immutable sources-of-truth for automation: serving-runtime /metrics, tenant-controller events, billing-collector aggregates.
- Minimize manual changes: use automation to propose adjustments; human approval for >10% or cross-tenant shifts.

High-level architecture (text diagram)
---
control-plane (tenant-metadata) --> reconciliation-service (cron) <-- billing-collector (aggregates)
                                            |
                                            v
                                     tenant-controller (quota-enforcer)
                                            |
                                            v
                                      serving-runtime (actual usage)

Telemetry anchors (data sources)
---
- serving-runtime:/metrics
  - per-tenant metrics: redwood_serving_tokens_per_minute, redwood_concurrent_sessions{tenant}, redwood_gpu_utilization_percent{device,tenant}
- tenant-controller:event-log (Kafka)
  - events: entitlement.update, entitlement.rollback, burst.grant, burst.reject
- billing-collector:hourly-aggregate (Postgres)
  - tables: tenant_hourly_usage(tenant_id, hour, tokens, gpu_hours, qps_p50)

Key metrics and recommended queries
---
- Current concurrency by tenant (PromQL):
  sum by (tenant) (redwood_concurrent_sessions{job="serving-runtime"})
- 15m sustained over-entitlement check (PromQL):
  max_over_time((sum by (tenant) (redwood_concurrent_sessions{job="serving-runtime"}) - tenant_entitlement_concurrency) [15m:1m]) > 0
- Burst credit balance (SQL):
  SELECT tenant_id, SUM(earned_credits - used_credits) AS balance FROM tenant_burst_ledger WHERE tenant_id = 'T-123' GROUP BY tenant_id;

Configuration matrix (thresholds and default values)
---
| config_key | default | description | owner |
| tenant_recon_interval | 01:00:00 | How often reconciliation runs (HH:MM:SS) | platform-sre |
| burst_window_minutes | 15 | Max duration of an automatic burst grant | platform-sre |
| burst_qps_multiplier | 1.5 | Max multiplier of configured QPS allowed in burst | product |
| overage_alert_pct | 10 | % over entitlement sustained before alerting | platform-sre |
| auto_adjust_threshold_pct | 5 | If observed median < entitlement - this % for 7d, propose downsizing | finance |

(Represented here as a pipe table for human readers; values live in config repo: infra/configs/private-deploy.yaml)

Reconciliation cadence and automation
---
1. Hourly reconciliation job (reconciliation-service cron every 1h): collect last 24h hourly aggregates from billing-collector and 5m metrics from serving-runtime.
2. Compute three signals per tenant:
   a. 24h median consumption vs entitlement
   b. 7d median and trend (up/down)
   c. Burst credit balance and recent burst frequency
3. Automation outcomes (ordered):
   - If observed > entitlement for >= 15m and burst credit available: auto-grant burst (see Burst admission).
   - If observed > entitlement and no credit / repeated violations (>=3 days): open P1 internal ticket to customer-success + SRE and begin manual review.
   - If observed < entitlement for 7d and savings > auto_adjust_threshold_pct: create a "proposal" PR against control-plane metadata repo with suggested entitlement decrement (human approval required).
4. Reconciliation events are stored in tenant_controller.event_log with tags: proposed_adjustment, burst_grant, enforcement_action.

Burst admission policy (automatic)
---
- Preconditions: burst_credit_balance > 0 AND node spare capacity (cluster-level slack > 10%).
- Max burst per tenant = min(config.burst_qps_multiplier * entitlement.qps, entitlement.qps + tenant_credit_tokens).
- Burst duration limited to config.burst_window_minutes.
- Grant action uses tenant-controller API: POST /v1/tenants/{id}/burst-grants with body {"duration_minutes": X, "max_qps": Y, "reason":"auto-recon"}.

Example burst grant CLI (field engineer debugging):
- curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/tenants/T-123/burst-grants \
  -d '{"duration_minutes":15, "max_qps":2000, "reason":"auto-recon"}'

Manual reconciliation runbook (when automation flags an issue)
---
1. Triage ticket created by reconciliation-service in platform queue with tags: tenant-id, signal, recommended-action.
2. SRE reviews telemetry anchors: 1m series for concurrency, last 24h billing-collector aggregates, and tenant_controller.event_log for recent entitlement writes.
3. If tenant shows a legitimate traffic spike (marketing/campaign): use the burst-grant API to issue a manual grant for requested duration. Notify Customer Success.
4. If tenant exhibits sustained overuse due to misconfiguration: rollback to last-known-good model or throttle specific endpoints via tenant-rate-limiter config. Steps:
   a. Identify offending route in serving-runtime traces (trace tags: tenant_id, route_id).
   b. Apply tenant-rate-limiter patch: PATCH /v1/tenants/{id}/rate-limits {"route_id":"/v1/generate","max_qps":X}
   c. Monitor for 10 minutes and escalate if errors spike.
5. If automation proposed entitlement downsize: verify customer contract and QBR notes before accepting the PR. Policy: never auto-decrease for enterprise customers without notification.

Capacity reallocation and soft-failback
---
- When cluster-level slack falls below 8% for 15m, reconciliation-service suspends all non-critical burst grants and emits alert: ClusterLowSlack.
- Soft-failback order (when reclaiming capacity):
  1. Revoke non-paying trial bursts (policy tag: trial=true)
  2. Revoke auto-grants older than 10 minutes
  3. Send 60s throttle to high-volume routes for offending tenants
  4. As last resort, invoke model-variant fallback to smaller quantized model for targeted tenants (controlled via rollout service).

Automation examples
---
CronJob (Kubernetes) example YAML (simplified):
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: tenant-reconciliation
spec:
  schedule: "0 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: recon
            image: redwood/recon-service:stable
            envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: private-deploy-config
          restartPolicy: OnFailure

Alerting and on-call actions
---
- Alerts (PagerDuty on-call):
  - ClusterLowSlack: severity=P0 -> page infra on-call immediately, run escalation steps in cluster-failure runbook.
  - TenantSustainedOverEntitlement: severity=P1 -> page tenant-owner SRE and CS via dedicated channel.
  - ReconciliationJobFailures: severity=P2 -> auto-create SRE ticket and retry job.

Auditability and evidence for customers
---
- Every reconciliation decision (auto or manual) must produce an exportable evidence bundle: {event_id, timestamp, observed_series, entitlement_snapshot, justification, actor}. This bundle is stored in control-plane.s3://private-recon-audit/{tenant}/{YYYY}/{event_id}.json
- For customers with restricted confidentiality: use signed manifests and KMS-encrypted blobs.

Templates and CSV formats
---
- Example CSV for manual entitlement adjustment proposals (header):
  tenant_id, current_qps, observed_7d_median_qps, proposed_qps, reason, proposal_owner, proposal_date
- Example ledger CSV (burst ledger):
  tenant_id, timestamp, change_type, credits_delta, reason, tx_id

Ownership and contact list
---
- Platform SRE: oncall-platform@redwood.ai (owner of reconciliation-service)
- Field Engineering: field-eng@redwood.ai (approvals for contract exceptions)
- Customer Success: cs-engagements@redwood.ai (customer communication and QBR notes)
- Finance (chargeback): finance-platform@redwood.ai (billing disputes and proposals)

Escalation matrix
---
1. SRE on-call (platform) — initial triage and temporary mitigation.
2. Field Eng — validate contract and approve any >10% entitlement changes.
3. CS Lead — notify customer and schedule follow-up.
4. Finance — ticket for billing adjustments if credits/overage apply.

Post-incident review and metrics to track
---
- Key success metrics after each reconciliation incident:
  - Time-to-detect (goal < 5m after 15m sustained signal)
  - Time-to-mitigate (goal < 20m for auto-burst, <60m for manual intervene)
  - False-positive rate of auto-grants (goal < 3% monthly)
  - Number of entitlement PRs created vs approved

Security and compliance notes
---
- All reconciliation jobs run with least privilege; service account tokens are short-lived and rotated via Vault.
- Audit bundles stored for minimum 90 days by default; extendable per customer contract.

---
